articles.title: Town's CEO on the self-organizing company
articles.author: Casey Newton

zh.thesis: AI 时代的公司不再需要人去维护知识库，自己的知识库可以自动生成。
paragraphs: Town 是一家新公司，刚拿到 a16z 的 5500 万美元投资。它做的是一个数字助理，叫 townie，能接入你的日历和邮箱，帮你准备会议、处理邮件。
但它真正有意思的地方在 onboarding 阶段。你连上邮箱和日历，它就会在几分钟内生成一个关于你的 wiki，包含你的工作内容、沟通风格、常用联系人。
这个 wiki 是助理的「记忆库」，它靠这个来办事。但对用户来说，它更像是一面镜子，让你第一次觉得 AI 真的认识你。
CEO 说，单人版只是开始。团队版很快会上线：每个员工的 townie 各自积累信息，然后自动汇总成公司的知识库。
难点在于隐私。如果每个员工的私人文件被混进去，AI 可能不小心把工资表放进公司共享库。他说那会「egg on face」，很尴尬。
他的解法分两步：短期靠产品设计，明令禁止提取个人邮箱的私密内容；长期靠专门训练过的模型，让 AI 自己执行公司的保密政策。
所以他认为，小公司会比大企业更早用上统一知识库。小团队人少信任高，风险可控，而大公司会被历史包袱拖住。

en.thesis: In the AI era, companies no longer need people to maintain knowledge bases; their own knowledge bases can be generated automatically.
paragraphs: Town is a new company that just received $55 million from a16z. It makes a digital assistant called townie that connects to your calendar and email, helping you prepare for meetings and handle messages.

But the really interesting part is the onboarding phase. Once you connect your email and calendar, it generates a wiki about you within minutes, covering your work, communication style, and frequent contacts.
This wiki is the assistant's 'memory bank' — that's what it relies on to get things done. But for the user, it feels more like a mirror, giving you the first sense that AI actually knows you.

The CEO says the single-user version is just the start. The team version is coming soon: each employee's townie accumulates information on its own, then automatically aggregates it into a company-wide knowledge base.
The challenge is privacy. If employees' private files get mixed in, the AI might accidentally put a salary sheet into the shared company library. He calls that 'egg on face' — embarrassing.

His solution has two parts. In the short term, product design forbids extracting sensitive content from personal email. In the long term, a specially trained model lets the AI enforce the company's own confidentiality policies.

So he thinks small companies will adopt a unified knowledge base earlier than big enterprises. Small teams have fewer people, more trust, and manageable risk, while big companies get weighed down by legacy baggage.

articles.title: Regulated Markets Are Slow to Handle Change
articles.author: Alex Tabarrok

zh.thesis: 监管原本为了防止电力公司过度建设而设的规则，在技术变革时期反而让它们死守旧电厂。
paragraphs: 美国电力公司长期按「回报率」监管：政府允许它们收回运营成本，再在资本上给一个合理回报。于是利润和资本规模挂钩，公司就有动力多建电厂，这被称为 Averch–Johnson 效应。
为了压制这种冲动，监管者要求资本必须「被使用且有用」。在稳定年代，这条规则还算有效，能挡住不少镀金工程。但技术一变，它就变味了。
页岩气革命让天然气发电成本暴跌。自由市场里，老煤电厂会因不划算被淘汰；可受监管的电力公司发现，只要继续烧煤，就能向监管者证明煤电厂「有用」，保住资本回报。
论文用美国各州数据验证了这一行为。在电力市场已放开的州，当煤价高于电价时，煤电厂明显减少发电；在受监管的州，煤电厂几乎不受价格影响。
更关键的是，受监管的州对天然气价格的反应其实并不迟钝——它们只是对煤价不敏感。因为「有用」标准盯住的是可能被淘汰的煤电，公司必须为煤辩护，而不是为气。
作者还建了结构模型，结论更糟：受监管的电力公司不仅挽留太多煤电，还新建了太多天然气电厂。旧资本和新资本同时过剩，Averch–Johnson 效应被放大了。
所以静态监管的规则，在动态技术变革中会失灵。作者暗示，与其这样监管，不如干脆放开市场。

en.thesis: Regulation meant to stop electric companies from overbuilding now traps them in old plants during technological change.
paragraphs: U.S. electric companies have long been regulated by 'rate of return': the government allows them to recover operating costs and then gives a reasonable return on capital. So profit is tied to the size of capital, and companies have an incentive to build more plants—this is called the Averch–Johnson effect.
To curb that impulse, regulators require that capital be 'used and useful.' In stable times, this rule works well and blocks many gold-plating projects. But when technology shifts, it turns sour.

The shale gas revolution made gas-fired power much cheaper. In a free market, old coal plants would be retired because they are uneconomical; but a regulated utility finds that as long as it keeps burning coal, it can prove to regulators that the coal plant is 'useful' and thus keep its capital return.

The paper verifies this behavior with data from U.S. states. In states where the electricity market is deregulated, when coal prices rise above electricity prices, coal plants clearly reduce output; in regulated states, coal plants are almost unaffected by price.

More importantly, regulated states are not actually slow to respond to natural gas prices—they are just insensitive to coal prices. Because the 'useful' standard focuses on coal power that might be retired, the company must defend coal, not gas.

The authors also build a structural model, and the conclusion is worse: regulated utilities not only keep too much coal power, but also build too many natural gas plants. Both old and new capital are excessive, and the Averch–Johnson effect is amplified.
So static regulation rules fail under dynamic technological change. The authors suggest that instead of this kind of regulation, it might be better to simply open the market.

articles.title: Why does Opus 5 feel worse to work with?
articles.author: numeri

zh.thesis: Opus 5 能力更强，但用起来更累，因为训练目标偏向基准测试，让它爱自作主张。
paragraphs: 在作者和他同事的体验里，Opus 5 用起来反而像降级。它明明更强，基准测试能追上 Fable，可就是不顺心。
问题出在它不主动问。旧模型遇到意图不清晰会停下来求确认，不会擅自假设，也不会改你的计划。Opus 5 全反着来。
作者怀疑这是两家力量逼出来的。一是各家都想造自我改进的 AI，想靠它自己递归升级；二是基准测试的分数压力太大。
基准题天生是能答的。它不给提示，也不要求你去猜作者的意图，只要按规则做就有标准答案。这就逼着模型在模糊处做大但大概率正确的假设。
可真实项目不是基准。上下文、意图、预算、业务影响，根本不可能全部写清楚交给代理。余下的模糊地带，宁可它停下来问一句。
作者并不指望能力退回去，只是希望交互上别再这么激进。现实生活没有标准答案，他不想要一个替你赌一把的代理。
所以各家在推强模型的时候，得把「什么时候该发问」也当一项能力来训练。光比谁答得快准，工作起来反而更心惊胆战。

en.thesis: Opus 5 is more capable, but it is more tiring to use, because its training targets benchmarks, which makes it act on its own.
paragraphs: In the experience of the author and his colleagues, Opus 5 feels like a downgrade. It is clearly stronger, its benchmarks can match Fable, but it is just not smooth.

The problem is that it does not actively ask. Older models would stop and ask for confirmation when the intent was unclear, they would not assume on their own, nor would they change your plan. Opus 5 does the opposite.
The author suspects this is forced by two forces. One is that everyone wants to build self-improving AI, hoping it can recursively upgrade itself; the other is the heavy pressure of benchmark scores.

Benchmark questions are inherently answerable. They give no hints, and they do not require you to guess the author's intent, you just follow the rules and there is a standard answer. This pushes the model to make big but likely correct assumptions in ambiguities.

But real projects are not benchmarks. Context, intent, budget, business impact, it is simply impossible to write all of it down and hand it to the agent. For the remaining ambiguous parts, better it stops and asks a question.
The author does not expect capability to regress, he just hopes the interaction will not be so aggressive. Real life has no standard answers, he does not want an agent that gambles for you.
So when companies push strong models, they have to train 'when to ask' as a capability too. Just competing on who answers fast and correctly makes work more frightening.

articles.title: History often hinges on boring technical questions
articles.author: Matthew Yglesias

zh.thesis: 货币政策的枯燥细节往往决定历史走向，比热门政治议题更值得关注。
paragraphs: 作者先从民主党缺乏全国议程说起，提议六项温和政策，比如禁止议员炒股、扩大医保覆盖牙科。但真正想谈的是更宏观的问题：经济政策的技术细节如何左右历史。
他举的第一个例子是 1874 年的通货膨胀法案。如果格兰特总统当时签署，注入更多绿背纸币，也许能缓解 1873 年恐慌后的通缩，民主党在中期选举就不会大胜，1876 年大选也可能避免争议，重建时期或许能延续更久。
虽然弗里德曼认为法案无关紧要，但另一些学者认为它能奏效。关键在于：货币政策的微调，可能改变整个国家的政治轨迹。
最震撼的例子是希特勒。1932 年德国深陷萧条，纳粹支持率飙升；如果布吕宁政府有更有效的货币应对，经济好转，纳粹或许不会上台。
2016 年也一样。如果耶伦当时不那么急于加息，克林顿可能多赢几票，美国历史就会不同。作者强调，经济繁荣是选举结果的关键变量。
所以政策制定者应该重视宏观经济的技术细节，而不是只关注热门议题。这也意味着，选民和评论家需要理解这些枯燥问题的重要性。
收尾：下次看到货币政策新闻，别跳过——它可能比表面上的政治争议更能决定未来。

en.thesis: The dull details of monetary policy often steer the course of history, and deserve more attention than flashy political issues.
paragraphs: The author starts by noting that Democrats lack a national agenda, and proposes six modest policies, like banning lawmakers from trading stocks and expanding dental coverage under Medicare. But what he really wants to talk about is something bigger: how the technical details of economic policy shape history.

His first example is the Inflation Act of 1874. If President Grant had signed it, putting more greenbacks into circulation, it might have eased the deflation after the Panic of 1873. Then the Democrats might not have won big in the midterms, the 1876 election might have avoided its dispute, and Reconstruction could have lasted longer.
Friedman thought the act didn't matter, but other scholars believe it could have worked. The key point is that a small tweak in monetary policy can change a whole nation's political path.

The most striking example is Hitler. In 1932 Germany was deep in depression and Nazi support was surging. If the Brüning government had had a more effective monetary response, the economy might have improved, and the Nazis might never have come to power.

It's the same in 2016. If Yellen had been less hasty to raise interest rates, Clinton might have won a few more votes, and U.S. history would be different. The author stresses that economic prosperity is the key variable in election outcomes.

So policymakers should pay attention to the technical details of macroeconomics, not just the hot topics. This also means voters and commentators need to understand how important these boring issues are.
To wrap up: next time you see a monetary policy headline, don't skip it—it might decide the future more than the political drama on the surface.

articles.title: I used Claude Fable 5 to rebuild my Nokia 3310 games, and it taught me how good those developers really were
articles.author: Abhinav Raj

zh.thesis: 用 AI 复刻童年游戏，反而让作者更佩服当年的诺基亚开发者。
paragraphs: 作者是 2000 年出生的，诺基亚 3310 正好在那年发布。他三岁起就偷玩父母手机上的 Space Impact 和 Snake II，记得手感却记不清细节。
好奇之下，他用 Claude Fable 5 仅凭童年记忆重建这两款游戏。Space Impact 被改名为 Void Runner，用 Python 和 Pygame 写的，五分钟后就能跑。
结果出乎意料：玩法结构、道具、甚至 BOSS 的走位模式都和他记忆里一样，让他想起当年躲在角落开枪的策略。
Snake II 变成 Neon Sprint，撞墙不死的设定、调节速度的选项、不同的迷宫，竟然全都被还原出来了。作者只给了游戏名，模型自己补充了细节。
作者说 Fable 5 一次就成功，而之前试过的 Gemini 3.1 Pro、GPT 5.5 和本地模型都需要反复引导。它几乎每一次都给出了正确的机制。
但更让他感慨的是游戏本身。那些游戏只占几 KB 内存，硬件几乎什么都没有，开发者却能设计出如此精妙又有趣的玩法。
所以 AI 的厉害在于重建，而当年的天才在于创造。理解设计容易，在匮乏中想出设计才是真本事。

en.thesis: Using AI to recreate childhood games made the author admire the original Nokia developers even more.
paragraphs: The author was born in 2000, and the Nokia 3310 came out that very year. He started sneaking plays on his parents' phone at age three, playing Space Impact and Snake II, remembering the feel but not the details.
Out of curiosity, he used Claude Fable 5 to rebuild both games from childhood memory alone. Space Impact became Void Runner, written in Python and Pygame, and it ran within five minutes.
The result surprised him: the gameplay structure, the power-ups, even the boss's movement patterns matched his memory exactly. It brought back the strategy of hiding in a corner and shooting.
Snake II became Neon Sprint. The no-wall-death rule, the speed adjustment option, the different mazes — all of it came back. He only gave the game name, and the model filled in the rest.
The author says Fable 5 succeeded on the first try, while Gemini 3.1 Pro, GPT 5.5, and local models all needed repeated prompting. It got the mechanics right almost every time.
But what struck him more was the games themselves. They took up only a few kilobytes of memory, the hardware had almost nothing, and yet the developers designed such clever, fun gameplay.
So AI is impressive at reconstruction, while the original genius lay in creation. Understanding a design is easy; coming up with one under scarcity is the real skill.

zh.thesis: 把生产力本身当爱好，会陷入不断换工具的循环，永远做不出作品。
paragraphs: 有些人把优化工作流当成乐趣：换个待办应用、试试新的 AI 助手、折腾笔记系统。他们觉得这是 harmless 的消遣，实际上是个陷阱。
真正的问题是，你是在「抽样」系统，而不是「建立」系统。每个新工具都带来希望，因为设置本身就让你感到前进，每次优化都刺激多巴胺。
但这个循环很快会结束：你宣布「这改变一切」，花几小时迁移数据，再到处推荐，直到遇到摩擦，然后发帖说再见，找下一个玩具。
彼得·德鲁克早在几十年前就点破了：多数人混淆了效率和效用。做得对的事，比把事做对更重要。而你的工具只教会你后者。
好用的工具最终会变得无趣——它们融入背景，不再占用你的注意力。对工作流感到无聊，其实是好事，说明该干活了。
别管社交网络上谁在吹什么新系统。挑一个哪怕笨拙的工具，坚持用到底。判断标准只有一个：它有没有让你产出作品。

en.thesis: Treating productivity itself as a hobby leads to an endless cycle of tool-switching, and you never actually make anything.
paragraphs: Some people get a kick out of optimizing their workflow: switching to-do apps, trying new AI assistants, fiddling with note systems. They think it's a harmless pastime, but it's actually a trap.

The real problem is that you're sampling systems, not building one. Every new tool brings hope, because the setup itself makes you feel like you're progressing, and each optimization gives a dopamine hit.
But the cycle soon ends: you declare 'this changes everything,' spend hours migrating data, then recommend it everywhere, until you hit friction, then post a farewell, and look for the next toy.
Peter Drucker pointed it out decades ago: most people confuse efficiency with effectiveness. Doing the right thing matters more than doing things right. And your tools only teach you the latter.
Good tools eventually become unremarkable—they fade into the background and stop occupying your attention. Being bored with your workflow is actually a good sign; it means it's time to get to work.
Forget whatever new system people are hyping on social media. Pick one tool, even if it's clumsy, and stick with it to the end. The only criterion: does it help you produce work?

articles.title: 科技爱好者周刊（第 408 期）：你需要知道的 AI 缓存知识

zh.thesis: 大模型的缓存命中价便宜五十倍，所以提示词的顺序值得专门设计。
paragraphs: 大模型的收费分输入和输出两部分，这个好理解。但价目表上还有第三项，叫「输入缓存命中价」。很多人扫过去就跳过了，其实它是省钱的关键。
以 DeepSeek V4 Flash 为例，命中缓存一次只要 2 分钱，没命中是 1 元。差了整整五十倍。
为什么差这么多？模型要把提示词拆成 Token，再算它们两两之间的注意力，这一步最耗算力。命中缓存就不必重算了，收的其实只是存储费。
所以多轮对话最划算。每一轮都要把之前的内容重新提交一遍，而那段前缀是不变的，模型可以直接取上次的结果。
但缓存有期限。DeepSeek 是 10 分钟，Anthropic 只有 5 分钟，OpenAI 在 10 到 30 分钟之间逐步失效。过期就得从头算，价格跳回 1 元。
于是 AI 工具会定时发请求保活。以前的做法是每 30 秒一次，十分钟就发 20 个请求，这笔钱也不少。
所以保活其实不用那么密。既然最短的缓存期限也有 5 分钟，每 4 分钟发一次就够了。

en.thesis: A cache hit costs one fiftieth of a miss, so prompt order is worth designing.
paragraphs: Model pricing splits into input and output, which is easy enough. But there is a third line on the price list, the input cache hit rate. Most people skim past it, and it is where the savings are.
On DeepSeek V4 Flash a hit costs two cents where a miss costs a full yuan. That is a factor of fifty.
Why the gap? The model has to split a prompt into tokens and compute attention between every pair of them, which is the expensive step. A hit skips it entirely, so what you pay for is storage.
That makes multi-turn conversation the best case. Every turn resubmits everything before it, and that prefix does not change, so the model can reuse what it already computed.
But caches expire. DeepSeek holds one for 10 minutes, Anthropic for 5, OpenAI decays between 10 and 30. Past that it recomputes and you are back to a yuan.
So agents send keep-alive requests. The old habit was one every 30 seconds, which is 20 requests across a quiet ten minutes and not free either.
Which means the pinging can be far lazier than that. The shortest cache anyone offers lasts five minutes, so once every four is enough.

articles.title: Intergenerational mobility of immigrants in 15 destination countries
articles.author: Tyler Cowen

zh.thesis: 移民子女的收入差距约一半来自父母收入，另一半来自目的地国家的劳动力市场和移民政策。
paragraphs: 新研究比较了 15 个国家的移民子女与本地人子女的收入。结果显示，移民子女的收入略低一些。
大约一半的差距可以用父母收入来解释：移民父母本身收入就低，子女自然受影响。另一半则是「流动性参数」的差异，也就是在同等父母收入下，移民子女的上升空间更小。
不过女儿的情况不一样。在多数目的地，移民女儿的收入反而高于本地人女儿。儿子的情况则分地区：在欧洲，移民儿子不如本地儿子；在欧洲以外，反而更好。
研究还发现，移民子女的绝对流动性跟父母的原籍国关系不大，主要是目的地国家的劳动力市场和移民政策在起作用。
换句话说，同样是移民，去哪个国家、当地政策怎样，比从哪里来更重要。

en.thesis: About half of the income gap for immigrant children comes from their parents' income; the other half comes from the labor market and immigration policy of the destination country.
paragraphs: A new study compares the incomes of immigrant children and native children in 15 countries. The results show that immigrant children earn a little less.

About half of the gap can be explained by parental income: immigrant parents themselves earn less, so their children are naturally affected. The other half is a difference in 'mobility parameters' — that is, given the same parental income, immigrant children have less room to move up.

But daughters are different. In most destinations, immigrant daughters actually earn more than native daughters. Sons split by region: in Europe, immigrant sons do worse than native sons; outside Europe, they do better.

The study also finds that the absolute mobility of immigrant children has little to do with their parents' country of origin. What matters is mainly the labor market and immigration policy of the destination country.
In other words, for the same immigrant, which country you go to and what the local policy is matters more than where you came from.

articles.title: The Economics of a Shrinking World
articles.author: Tyler Cowen

zh.thesis: 全球生育率首次降到更替水平以下，且下降集中在穷国和低教育女性，说明是现代化本身在压低生育，而非单一因素。
paragraphs: 2026 年，人类可能首次低于更替生育率。以前战争和瘟疫都没做到，这个变化是头一遭。
更让人意外的是，下降集中在低收入和中等收入国家，而且是穷人和教育程度低的女性。不是我们以为的富裕国家先降。
研究者用单一因素模型拟合了 236 国 1950 年以来的数据。共同因素在 1978 年见顶，此后一路向下，但各国自己的趋势才是主因，219 个为负，没有一个开始平稳。
常见解释——收入、教育、城市化——都说不通这个模式。论文提出一个猜测：现代化本身让第三个孩子变贵，让无孩变得便宜。
孩子是整数，所以一点微小变化就能让生育率从 1.8 掉到 1.3。而且经济里没有一股力量会把它推回 2.1。
后果主要是增长变慢。人口少了，劳动力、创新、市场规模都会缩。
作者 Tyler Cowen 提醒，别忽视避孕手段的作用，尽管有滞后。真正的普及比表面看起来更难。所以这事没有回头路，只能适应一个缩小的世界。

en.thesis: Global fertility is falling for the first time below replacement level, and the decline is concentrated in poor countries and among less educated women, which suggests modernization itself is lowering fertility, not any single factor.
paragraphs: In 2026, humanity may fall below replacement fertility for the first time. Wars and plagues never did that, so this is a first.
What is more surprising is that the decline is concentrated in low- and middle-income countries, and among poor and less educated women. It is not the rich countries we expected to lead the fall.

Researchers fit a single-factor model to data from 236 countries since 1950. The common factor peaked in 1978 and has been falling ever since, but each country's own trend is the main driver: 219 are negative, and none has started to level off.
Common explanations—income, education, urbanization—cannot account for this pattern. The paper offers a guess: modernization itself makes a third child more expensive and childlessness cheaper.
Children are indivisible, so a tiny shift can drop fertility from 1.8 to 1.3. And there is no force in the economy to push it back up to 2.1.
The main consequence is slower growth. With fewer people, labor, innovation, and market size all shrink.
Author Tyler Cowen reminds us not to ignore the role of contraception, although there is a lag. Real普及 is harder than it looks. So there is no turning back; we can only adapt to a shrinking world.

articles.title: “To Write Well is to Think Clearly”: David McCullough
articles.author: conversableeconomist

zh.thesis: 写作就是思考，想不清楚就写不清楚，所以写作训练不能被砍掉。
paragraphs: David McCullough 是两度普利策奖得主，写过《杜鲁门》和《约翰·亚当斯》，也写过《布鲁克林大桥》《怀特兄弟》这些畅销书。他本人就是靠写作思考的典范。
2002 年他接受访谈时说，学校砍掉艺术经费是错的。艺术只能靠做来学，弹琴要上手弹，写作要动手写，思考也一样，不写就不会想。
他有一句常被引用的话：写作就是思考，写得好就是想得清楚。正因如此，写作才那么难。
他特别强调「把想法写在纸上」这句老话——笔有让大脑聚焦的奇效，别的工具都比不上。所以他主张各科都要多写，历史课也该批改学生的文章，不只是语文课。
这段话说的是学习方法，也是在说教育政策。他觉得写作训练是思考能力的根基，砍掉它，学生失去的不只是表达技巧。
所以这份访谈的真正主张是：写作不是选修课，而是思维的必修课。想清楚和写清楚是同一件事的两面，练写作就是在练脑子。

en.thesis: Writing is thinking: if you can't think clearly, you can't write clearly, so writing training should not be cut.
paragraphs: David McCullough is a two-time Pulitzer winner, author of 'Truman' and 'John Adams', as well as bestsellers like 'The Brooklyn Bridge' and 'The Wright Brothers'. He is himself a model of thinking through writing.

In a 2002 interview, he said that cutting arts funding in schools was wrong. The arts can only be learned by doing: to play piano you must actually play, to write you must actually write, and thinking is the same — without writing, you won't think.
He has a often-quoted line: writing is thinking, and to write well is to think clearly. That is precisely why writing is so hard.

He stressed the old saying 'putting ideas down on paper' — the pen has a remarkable power to focus the mind that no other tool matches. So he argued that all subjects should involve more writing; even history classes should grade students' essays, not just language arts.
This is about learning methods, but also about education policy. He sees writing training as the foundation of thinking ability; cutting it means students lose more than just expression skills.

So the real argument of this interview is: writing is not an elective but a required course for thinking. Thinking clearly and writing clearly are two sides of the same coin, and practicing writing is practicing the mind.

articles.title: How Will the 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act Affect Housing Supply? Part II
articles.author: Brian Potter

zh.thesis: 新住房法案里最有分量的条款只集中在少数几条，能增加多少供给很难说。
paragraphs: 美国刚通过的《21世纪住房之路法案》有三章，这篇拆的是后两章：第二章讲怎么多建房，第三章讲怎么推广预制房。
第二章有十三项条款，多数只是调整资金分配，不增加总量。比如给机会区加分、扩大银行投资上限，这些都不改变总盘子。
真正可能改变供给的是几项：创新基金每年拨款 2 亿美元奖励建房增速快的地区；RAD 计划扩容 10 万套公屋，允许其改建；还有简化环评审查。
RAD 扩容可能是最实的。公屋转成住房券项目后，就能拿未来的补贴收入做抵押，借钱维修。纽约的 Fulton 项目就是在拆旧建新时多盖了 3454 套。
第三章关于预制房，最受关注的是取消永久钢底盘。它占预制房成本 5% 到 10%，但作者怀疑省下的钱未必能刺激多少人购买。因为预制房已经够便宜，瓶颈不在价格。
还有一项要求研究模块化建筑的融资障碍，但只要求研究，不强制改革，而且 HUD 早在 1974 年就有权改。作者判断基本没有影响。
所以整体看，这是典型的联邦立法：大部分条款是给现有项目换个名字，真正能增加供给的只有那四五条。而它们的实际效果，取决于那些约束到底卡得多紧——这点谁也说不准。

en.thesis: The new housing bill's most weighty provisions are concentrated in just a few sections, and whether they can increase supply is anyone's guess.
paragraphs: The just-passed 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act has three chapters. This piece looks at the last two: the second chapter on how to build more homes, the third on promoting prefab housing.

Chapter two has thirteen provisions, but most just adjust how money is distributed without adding to the total. For example, giving preference to opportunity zones or raising the cap on bank investment—none of these changes the overall pie.

What might actually shift supply are a few items: an innovation fund with $200 million a year to reward regions that speed up construction; the RAD program expanding to 100,000 public housing units and allowing their conversion; and streamlining environmental reviews.

The RAD expansion is probably the most concrete. Once public housing converts to a voucher program, it can borrow against future subsidy income to finance repairs. New York's Fulton project added 3,454 units while tearing down and rebuilding.

Chapter three deals with prefab homes, and the most watched change is removing the permanent steel chassis. It makes up 5% to 10% of the cost of a prefab home, but the author doubts the savings will spur much buying. Because prefab homes are already cheap enough, the bottleneck isn't price.

There's also a provision requiring a study of financing barriers for modular construction, but it only asks for a study, not mandatory reform, and HUD has had the power to change things since 1974. The author judges it to have essentially no impact.

So overall, this is typical federal legislation: most provisions just rebrand existing programs, and only four or five actually add supply. And their real effect depends on how tightly those constraints bite—which no one can say for sure.

zh.thesis: 一周的乐观清单里，真正值得记住的是 Fuse 在聚变效率上的突破，它可能让聚变电站更早到来。
paragraphs: 这是 Not Boring 的每周乐观清单，汇总了几条科技和商业新闻。领头的是 Avidrone 赢得 DARPA 重型无人机挑战，载重达到自身重量 3.84 倍，但最终尝试 4 倍时坠毁了。
还有 Josh Kushner 和 Bob Iger 以 125 亿美元收购湖人队，创下 NBA 球队价格纪录。文章借此聊了稀缺资产：科技公司每周都有新实验室，但湖人只有一个。
天气控制赛道出现了第二家创业公司 Recast，它用 AI 和高性价比的播云材料，为政府和科学家提供定向播云服务。作者看好整个领域，认为会百花齐放。
最硬的干货是聚变公司 Fuse 的新纪录：FAETON-X 单次产生 1.27×10¹² 个中子，比劳伦斯利弗莫尔实验室效率更高。诀窍在于电流效率，它提高 40%，产出的中子按四次方暴涨。
Fuse 的策略是先用中子照射服务赚钱，再迭代技术冲向聚变发电。它九个月从设计到首秀，再九个月破纪录，走一条比同行更务实的路线。
清单最后是 Matic 扫地机器人新增语音控制，可以喊它跟着你，或者让它去打扫客厅。作者认为这种单点实用机器人比人形机器人更可能先进家庭。
所以这篇是乐观资本的合集，每条都能点燃对未来的想象。但真正值得跟进的是 Fuse 的效率曲线，它让聚变发电从实验室走向商业的时间线缩短了。

en.thesis: This week's optimism list, but the real takeaway is Fuse's breakthrough in fusion efficiency, which could bring fusion power plants closer.
paragraphs: This is Not Boring's weekly dose of optimism, rounding up a few tech and business stories. Leading is Avidrone winning DARPA's heavy-lift drone challenge, carrying 3.84 times its own weight, though it crashed on a final attempt at 4 times.

Also Josh Kushner and Bob Iger bought the Lakers for $12.5 billion, a record for an NBA team. The piece reflects on scarce assets: tech companies open new labs every week, but there is only one Lakers.

Weather control has a second startup, Recast, which uses AI and cheap cloud-seeding materials for targeted cloud seeding for governments and scientists. The author is bullish on the whole field and expects many players.

The hard core is fusion company Fuse's new record: FAETON-X produced 1.27×10¹² neutrons in one shot, more efficient than Lawrence Livermore. The trick is current efficiency, up 40%, which boosts neutron output to the fourth power.

Fuse's strategy is to first make money with neutron irradiation services, then iterate toward fusion power. It went from design to first shot in nine months, then broke records in another nine, a more pragmatic path than peers.

The list closes with Matic's robot vacuum adding voice control, so you can tell it to follow you or clean the living room. The author thinks such single-purpose practical robots are more likely to enter homes than humanoids.

So this is a collection of optimistic capital, each item sparking imagination. But the real one to follow is Fuse's efficiency curve, which shortens the timeline for fusion power to go from lab to commercial.

articles.title: 3 myths about coding with AI that even experienced developers still believe
articles.author: Abhinav Raj

zh.thesis: AI 写代码并没有让开发者更轻松，只是把时间从写代码换成了查代码。
paragraphs: AI 编程助手火了四年，很多开发者以为它省下时间，自己就能专心做高层次的思考。但奥克兰大学的研究发现，事情没那么简单。
82% 的程序员承认写代码的时间变少了，可省下的时间都花在验证、评估和改 AI 的输出上。84% 的人觉得 AI 提高了效率，但抱怨体验变差的人翻了一倍，从 14% 涨到 27%。
损失最明显的是心流状态和认知负荷。写得更少不等于干得更少，AI 省下的时间并没有自动变成高级思考。
第二个迷思是 AI 代码审查能抓到人类漏掉的安全漏洞。多伦多都会大学的研究测试了 GitHub Copilot 的代码审查，发现它经常漏掉 SQL 注入、跨站脚本这类关键漏洞，倒是爱挑剔代码风格和拼写。
所以专家们还是建议保留人工代码审计。AI 的眼睛可能没在看该看的地方。
但说 AI 编码只是高级自动补全也不对。Claude Code 和 Codex CLI 已经能推理、改多个文件、跑测试，还能自主迭代。Epoch AI 和 METR 的测试里，Claude Opus 4.6 自己重写了一个 1.6 万行 Go 的生物信息学工具包，通过了 2001 个测试，估计要人类工程师做 2 到 17 周。
所以真相是：AI 确实能干活，但它改变的是工作内容，不是工作总量。它把创建换成了验证，把心流换成了监控，好不好用，取决于你更讨厌哪种累。

en.thesis: AI coding doesn't make developers' lives easier; it just swaps writing code for checking code.
paragraphs: AI coding assistants have been around for four years, and many developers think the time they save lets them focus on higher-level thinking. But research from the University of Auckland finds it's not that simple.

82% of programmers admit they spend less time writing code, but the saved time goes into verifying, evaluating, and fixing AI output. 84% feel AI boosts efficiency, yet the share complaining about worse experience doubled, from 14% to 27%.
The biggest loss is in flow state and cognitive load. Writing less isn't doing less; the time AI saves doesn't automatically become deep thinking.

The second myth is that AI code review can catch security holes that humans miss. A study from Toronto Metropolitan University tested GitHub Copilot's code review and found it often misses critical flaws like SQL injection and cross-site scripting, while being picky about style and spelling.
So experts still recommend keeping human code audits. AI's eyes may not be looking where they should.

But calling AI coding just advanced autocomplete is wrong too. Claude Code and Codex CLI can already reason, edit multiple files, run tests, and iterate on their own. In tests by Epoch AI and METR, Claude Opus 4.6 rewrote a 16,000-line Go bioinformatics toolkit on its own, passing 2,001 tests, which would take a human engineer an estimated 2 to 17 weeks.

So the truth is: AI can indeed do real work, but it changes the nature of the work, not the total amount. It swaps creation for verification, flow for monitoring. Whether it's worth it depends on which kind of tired you hate more.

zh.thesis: 印度人模仿长尾猴叫声驱赶猕猴，成了德里办赛前的新工种，这反映了服务业的弹性。
paragraphs: 模仿长尾猴的尖叫声，听起来不像能赚钱的技能，但在印度，这确实成了一门工作，甚至是一种职业。
这些靠嗓子吃饭的人，专门负责驱赶猴子。德里要办羽毛球世锦赛，但城里到处是恒河猴，偷东西、捣乱，赶不走。
长尾猴的叫声是唯一有效的威慑。恒河猴一听，以为是天敌来了，就跑了。于是主办方雇了一批「人形长尾猴」。
这活儿听着滑稽，但说明服务业能创造意想不到的岗位。需求来了，技能就跟着长出来。
不过文章只当趣闻转述，没有讨论这工种是否长久、值多少钱。读者能带走的就是一个有趣的例子。

en.thesis: Mimicking the langur's cry to scare off monkeys has become a new job in Delhi before the tournament, which shows the service sector's flexibility.
paragraphs: Imitating the shrill cry of a langur doesn't sound like a skill that can earn money, but in India it has indeed become a job, even a profession.

These people, who earn a living with their voices, are specifically hired to drive away monkeys. Delhi is hosting the badminton world championships, but the city is full of rhesus macaques that steal things and cause trouble, and they won't leave.
The langur's call is the only effective deterrent. When rhesus macaques hear it, they think their natural enemy is coming and run away. So the organizers hired a bunch of 'human langurs'.
This work sounds ridiculous, but it shows that the service sector can create unexpected jobs. When demand arises, skills grow accordingly.
However, the article merely recounts it as an amusing anecdote and does not discuss whether this job will last or how much it pays. What the reader can take away is just an interesting example.

zh.thesis: 对于自动化 AI 研发的风险，我们不必坐等危机，现在有 23 项低后悔成本的政策可以开始准备。
paragraphs: AI 公司员工联名呼吁政府给前沿 AI 研发踩刹车，但作者觉得刹车太重了，不如先做准备。他们列了 23 项政策，覆盖透明度、情报、电网等七个领域。
这些政策有个共同点：就算 AI 风险后来没发生，也不亏。比如资助生物防御、加固电网、保护模型权重，平时也有用。
透明度方面，作者建议公开 AI 研发自动化的信息，比如公司内部用了多少 AI 做研发、出了哪些事故。这能帮政府和公众提前看清趋势。
验证技术是重头戏。现在全世界做这件事的人不到 50 个，作者建议建联盟、办竞赛、造一个完全可验证的数据中心。有了它，美中才有可能互相信任地限制最危险的 AI 活动。
竞争方面，美国算力领先中国十倍，但作者认为可以拉到一百倍以上。堵住芯片走私、防止蒸馏模型能力、保护模型权重，都能扩大优势。
电网和数据中心也是瓶颈。作者建议简化审批、建特殊工业区，让社区同意建数据中心，换取税收和教育投入。
这些建议不加总则，只谈准备。作者承认无法确定要不要给 AI 踩刹车，但认为先把工具箱备好，比到时候手忙脚乱强。

en.thesis: We don't have to wait for a crisis to act on the risks of automated AI R&D: there are 23 low-regret policies we can start preparing now.
paragraphs: AI company employees have jointly called on governments to put the brakes on frontier AI development, but the authors think that braking is too heavy; better to prepare first. They list 23 policies covering seven areas including transparency, intelligence, and the power grid.

These policies have something in common: even if the AI risks never materialize, there is no loss. For instance, funding biodefense, hardening the grid, and protecting model weights are useful in normal times too.

On transparency, the authors suggest making public information about the automation of AI R&D, such as how much AI companies use internally for R&D and what accidents have occurred. This can help governments and the public see trends in advance.

Verification technology is a big item. Fewer than 50 people in the world do this now, and the authors suggest building a coalition, holding competitions, and building a fully verifiable data center. With that, the US and China could trust each other enough to restrict the most dangerous AI activities.

On competition, the US has ten times China's computing power, but the authors believe it can be pushed to over a hundred times. Blocking chip smuggling, preventing model distillation, and protecting model weights can all widen the gap.

The grid and data centers are also bottlenecks. The authors suggest simplifying approvals and creating special industrial zones, letting communities agree to data centers in exchange for tax and educational investments.

These suggestions impose no moratorium, only preparation. The authors admit they cannot be sure whether to put the brakes on AI, but think it is better to have the toolbox ready than to scramble when the time comes.
